steps.prompt: How does one prompt become a finished video?
steps.sub: Faceless AI "slop" and a video that actually lands look the same at a glance — but one is assembled with intent. By the end you'll be able to name every stage of the pipeline and say what each one adds.

steps.prompt: First instinct — what is an AI video pipeline, really?

options.t: One magic model that takes a topic and outputs a finished MP4.
An assembly line of stages — script, voice, visuals, captions, music — each making one file, then composited together.
A folder of stock clips you stitch together by hand.

steps.why: There's no single button. A pipeline is an assembly line: each stage produces one ingredient (a script, a narration WAV, visuals, a caption track, a music bed), and a final compositing step layers them on one timeline and renders the MP4. Thinking in stages is what lets you fix or upgrade any one part without redoing the whole thing.
hints: If it were one magic model, you couldn't swap the voice without redoing the visuals. Can you?
Each stage hands its output to the next — like a factory line, not a single machine.

steps.sub: Tap each card. These six, in order, turn an idea into a video.

cards.b: The words. The spine everything else syncs to. No good script, no good video.
TTS turns the script into clear human-sounding narration — no mic, no voice actor.
Per-scene backgrounds, footage, or motion graphics that match what's being said.
Word-synced on-screen text. Most viewers watch muted — this keeps them following.
A soft bed under the voice that sets emotion without burying the narration.
Compositing layers every element on one timeline and renders the final MP4.

steps.prompt: Put the pipeline stages in the order they run.
steps.sub: Tap them from first to last. One feeds the next.
chips: Turn the script into AI narration
Lay a soft music bed under the voice
hints: Everything syncs to the words — so what has to exist first?
Captions and visuals both follow the narration's timing; compositing is always last because it needs all the pieces.

steps.prompt: What does each stage actually ADD? Sort each job.
steps.sub: Tap a job, then the stage it belongs to.

items.t: Lets muted viewers follow every word
Gives the video a human narrator with no mic
Sets the emotional tone without competing with the voice
Keeps eyes on screen by matching the words to what's shown

hints: One of these is about sound under the talking; one is about text on top of it.
Visuals hold attention with the eyes; captions hold attention for the muted; music holds the mood.

steps.prompt: Walk one scene through the stack.
steps.sub: You're making a 60-second short, "Why your phone battery dies fast." Pick the next move at each stage.
steps.goal: Turn the topic into a finished, watchable scene.

turns.situation: You have a topic and a blank timeline. Nothing else exists yet.
options: The script line for this scene
turns.log: 📝 Script → "Lithium batteries hate heat — here's why."

turns.situation: The script line is written. You need a narrator but have no mic.
options: Run the line through TTS to get narration audio
Add captions before there's any audio

turns.situation: You have a 4.2s narration clip. The screen is still blank.
turns.q: What does the scene need now?
options: A visual that matches "battery + heat" for these 4.2s
Another copy of the same audio
turns.log: 🎨 Visuals → close-up of a warm phone, 4.2s

turns.situation: Script, voice, and visuals exist as separate files. Muted viewers see nothing readable.
turns.q: What two layers finish the scene before render?
options: Word-synced captions, then a soft music bed

turns.situation: All four ingredients are aligned on the timeline.
options: Composite all layers and render the MP4

hints: Follow the same order as the cards: script → voice → visuals → captions → music → render.
Compositing is last because it needs every other piece to already exist.

steps.prompt: Myth-check the stack — true or false?
steps.sub: Tap True or False for each, then check all at once.

statements.t: The script is just a starting note — the rest of the pipeline can ignore it.
statements.why: False — the script is the spine. Voice reads it, captions are its words, visuals and music are timed to it. A weak script makes every later stage weaker.

statements.t: You can swap the music bed without re-rendering the voice or visuals.
statements.why: True — because each stage produces a separate file, you can change one ingredient and re-composite. That modularity is the whole point of thinking in stages.

statements.t: Compositing happens first, before you have any of the pieces.
statements.why: False — compositing is last. It layers the script-driven voice, visuals, captions, and music onto one timeline and renders the MP4. It needs the pieces to exist first.

statements.t: Captions and a music bed both raise watch-time, but in different ways.
statements.why: True — captions keep muted viewers reading along (retention + accessibility); a soft music bed holds emotional tone so people don't drop off in silence.

hints: Trace the dependencies: what does each later stage need from an earlier one?
Modularity means separate files — change one, re-composite, done.

steps.prompt: A creator's video has crisp voice, slick captions, and music — but viewers drop off in the first 10 seconds. Which stage is most likely the real problem?
steps.sub: Think about what every other stage depends on.

options.t: The render quality — bump the resolution.
The script — if the words don't hook, polish on the other stages can't save it.

steps.why: Production polish can't rescue a weak opening. Voice, visuals, captions, and music all amplify the script — if the words don't earn the first 10 seconds, there's nothing to amplify. The stack makes a good idea shine; it can't manufacture one.
hints: Louder music or higher resolution won't fix a boring first line.
Every stage is downstream of the words. Fix the source, not the symptoms.

steps.prompt: Build the stack: tap ALL the stages that belong in an AI video pipeline.
steps.sub: A couple of these sound techy but aren't stages of the pipeline. Pick only the real ones.
steps.why: The stack is Script → Voice → Visuals → Captions → Music → Render. A subscriber count and a color palette matter for a channel, but neither is a stage that produces an ingredient of the video itself.
hints: Recall the six cards you opened — those are the stages.
If it doesn't produce a file that gets composited into the video, it's not a pipeline stage.
